visual_text.rest: of Hôtel du Cap-Eden-Roc wins the world blind tasting title for France.

post_text:
Camille Guilbaud, 30, sommelier at Hôtel du Cap-Eden-Roc, is now a world champion of blind tasting.

With her teammate Candy Sangare, founder of Art de Vivre by Candy, she won the 14th World Blind Tasting Championship for France, in Avignon on 17 October. The pair scored 189 points, ahead of Japan on 181 and Brazil on 159. The decider was the twelfth wine, a Sercial Madeira that Japan took for a Boal.

It is France's fifth world title, its second in a row, and the first won by an all-female French team. Guilbaud joined the Oetker hotel about three years ago. Its cellar holds more than 5,000 references.

A second title went to a Paris palace. Dimitri Nalin, head sommelier at Hôtel Barrière Fouquet's Paris, won the French edition of the Ruinart Sommelier Challenge 2026 on 26 October, at Cheval Blanc Paris. Ruinart cellar master Caroline Fiot and sommelier Estelle Touzet sat on the jury.

The signal: in a palace, the wine team is now a reason to book, not a back-office skill. A titled sommelier is a story guests, critics and future recruits all hear.
